families.name: Infrastructure
families.blurb: The boring, load-bearing ones. Backups, exposed ports, latency, fleet health.

families.name: The Pulse Suite
families.blurb: One visual language for what the machine is doing to itself. Pulse carries CPU, memory, storage and network in one icon; sound and battery keep their own.

families.name: The AI Desk
families.blurb: What the agents on this machine are actually doing, and what they are costing.

families.name: Workspace Control
families.blurb: Hyprland workspaces that name themselves, pack themselves, and remember what belonged on them.

families.name: Media and Output
families.blurb: Sound and pixels leaving this machine for somewhere else in the house.

families.name: System and Desk
families.blurb: Everyday surfaces. Clipboard, clock, bluetooth, sleep, the car.

families.name: The Mac Bridge
families.blurb: Your phone and your Mac, in the Linux bar. The Mac is the gateway, this machine is the client, nothing is proxied through a stranger.

plugins.name: LANarchy
plugins.tagline: Your homelab, drawn as it actually is.
plugins.description: Homelab topology map and health in the Omarchy bar: every machine and service, UniFi detail, and measured traffic on the links that carry it. Map, list and flow views, with hosts you curate sitting alongside the ones discovery finds. Hard-forked from Donnie Fiander's Lanarchy, which is credited throughout.

plugins.name: Trackpad Pulse
plugins.tagline: Your trackpad, in motion.
plugins.description: A live trackpad on the bar that lights where your fingers are, and behind it every number the pad can give: touches, taps, gestures, palms, speed and distance on every clock, a heatmap, a week of history. A finger-speed map drawn under the acceleration curve with an optimizer that fits the curve to your hand and keeps watching. Hyprland gestures for three and four fingers with themes and backgrounds in the mix, and a weekly report that knows which hand you use. Built on David Fano's Trackpad Plus, kept whole.

plugins.name: OmaGuard
plugins.tagline: Knows what your desktop looked like when it was right.
plugins.description: A shield in the bar that captures your Hyprland and Omarchy config on a timeline, tells you when something drifted from the state you accepted, and shows a precise before and after for putting one value back, as a preview, never an automatic write. Also saves and quick-switches whole bar layouts.

plugins.name: RAM Speed Test
plugins.tagline: Memory read and write, on the speed test dials.
plugins.description: Sustained multi-core memory copy and triad throughput, drawn on the same gauge cluster as Omarchy's built-in network and disk speed tests, with thread scaling, pressure checks and JSON reports. Summon it from the launcher or with omarchy-shell shell summon nixfred.ram-speedtest.

plugins.name: Pulse
plugins.tagline: One icon showing whatever is holding the machine back.
plugins.description: CPU, memory, storage and network merged into a single bar widget with one shared severity model. The icon follows the biggest constraint rather than a fixed metric, and each domain still opens the full dashboard the separate plugin had. Replaces CPU Pulse, RAM Pulse, Disk Pulse and Net Pulse.
plugins.supersedes: CPU Pulse, RAM Pulse, Disk Pulse, Net Pulse

plugins.name: PR Hunter
plugins.tagline: Open pull requests, and the workspace to deal with them.
plugins.description: GitHub pull requests and issues for Herdr and your saved projects, in the bar. Opens the right workspace or terminal and hands the work to an agent that is already running.

plugins.name: MenuBar Overload
plugins.tagline: Add as many plugins as you like.
plugins.description: The Omarchy bar with a dock-magnified carousel on each side. Add as many plugins as you like; roll through the ones that do not fit with the mouse wheel or a trackpad swipe, and each one pops out as it arrives.

plugins.name: Audio Pulse
plugins.tagline: A living audio chip.
plugins.description: A living audio chip: volume, mute, output picker and per-app mixer, drawn as a sibling of RAM Pulse, CPU Pulse and Net Pulse.

plugins.name: Power Pulse
plugins.tagline: Battery as a glowing flux cell whose colour is its charge.
plugins.description: Battery as a glowing flux cell whose colour is its charge: blue when full, yellow in the middle, red when low. A stream of glowing atoms rides in while charging, out on battery, with glints popping around them. Hour-long up and down power trace, live wattage, power profiles.

plugins.name: Sonomarchy
plugins.tagline: Every Sonos zone as a system audio output.
plugins.description: Makes every Sonos zone on your network a selectable system audio output, including legacy Play:1, Play:3, Play:5, Playbar and Connect speakers that have no AirPlay.

plugins.name: Chronos
plugins.tagline: A clock and calendar with a pulse.
plugins.description: Clock and calendar with a pulse: a day-progress ring, shimmering year and life rails, a drawn moon phase, and a month grid that arrives on a stagger.

plugins.name: Pastey
plugins.tagline: A clipboard that remembers.
plugins.description: A compact, searchable 200-item clipboard history for the Omarchy bar, with real screenshot thumbnails and the whole clip on hover.

plugins.name: Burn Bar
plugins.tagline: A thermal heat map of what the AIs are costing you.
plugins.description: Live thermal heat map of the AIs this machine actually uses, Claude, Codex, Grok, and local Ollama when a GPU is present, with weekly quota gauges and the share of tokens kept off frontier models.

plugins.name: Backup Sizzle
plugins.tagline: Restic, with a countdown ring and an outcome calendar.
plugins.description: Restic backup with live B2 throughput, countdown ring, outcome calendar, anomaly notes, snapshot browser and run history.

plugins.name: Beatdeck
plugins.tagline: A live spectrum that opens a media cockpit.
plugins.description: Beatbar's live spectrum as the trigger for the Living Media Cockpit. Click for now playing, right click for the visuals.

plugins.name: Halo Bluetooth
plugins.tagline: A live sonar hero with battery halos.
plugins.description: Bluetooth with a live sonar hero, per-device battery halos and type-aware glyphs.

plugins.name: Tesla
plugins.tagline: Your car in the bar.
plugins.description: Your Tesla in the bar: where it is, how full it is, how far that gets you, and whether it is charging right now.

plugins.name: Blip
plugins.tagline: iMessage in the Omarchy bar.
plugins.description: iMessage in the Omarchy bar. Reads and sends through a Mac you own over a multiplexed SSH socket. iMessage is macOS-only, so this machine is a thin client and the Mac is the gateway. The bar badge counts every unread; desktop toasts fire only for handles on your allowlist, because chat.db is mostly bank alerts and 2FA codes.

plugins.name: Tailscale Host Monitor
plugins.tagline: Your whole tailnet, from the bar.
plugins.description: Select nodes from your Tailscale network, track every device type, and collect deep Linux metrics over read-only SSH.

plugins.name: Internet Latency
plugins.tagline: Live color-coded latency, with the loss and jitter behind it.
plugins.description: Live color-coded internet latency with target selection, packet loss, jitter, and history.

plugins.name: Infomarchy
plugins.tagline: Your wallpaper becomes a live information desk.
plugins.description: A live, clickable wallpaper desk for AI sessions, proactive next-action alerts, repository health, Ollama controls, activity, usage limits, and machine telemetry. Theme-driven, on a SUPER+D overlay.

plugins.name: Workspace Names
plugins.tagline: Numbers stay numbers. Now they have a name too.
plugins.description: Give Hyprland workspaces a title without touching their numbers. Workspaces name themselves from their windows until you rename them. Includes inline rename and a live Workspace Map with occupancy and app identities.

plugins.name: Plonk
plugins.tagline: Workspaces close their own gaps.
plugins.description: Packs numeric Hyprland workspaces into 1 through N as gaps appear, preserving order, tiling, monitor placement, and focus.

plugins.name: Rift
plugins.tagline: Hyprland tiles, Rift remembers.
plugins.description: Save the applications on a workspace as a named Rift and reopen them on demand or at login, straight from the Omarchy bar. No geometry is saved, so Hyprland keeps tiling.

plugins.name: Apple Notes
plugins.tagline: Apple Notes, read and written from Linux.
plugins.description: A safety-first Apple Notes browser for Omarchy, using a Mac you own as the private source. Search, read, create, and safely append over a confined SSH bridge.

themes.name: 2 Hackrz
themes.tagline: Midnight blue, muted steel, warm terminal.
themes.description: A midnight-blue Omarchy Quattro theme with muted steel accents and warm terminal colors.

tools.name: LightShow
tools.description: Keyboard RGB for MSI MysticLight laptops on Linux. A GTK4 app with 20 effects, live theme matching and day and night profiles. No vendor software, no Windows.

tools.name: Imprint
tools.description: Stamp one Omarchy machine onto another.

tools.description: Voice recorder with live whisper.cpp transcription for Omarchy. GTK4 and PipeWire.

tools.name: Clipsync
tools.description: One clipboard across Linux, macOS and iPhone. Copy anywhere, paste on Linux, text and photos.

tools.name: Swish
tools.description: macOS Cmd+Tab for Omarchy. Hold SUPER, tab through glass workspace cards with live preview.

tools.description: Teach Claude Code to use the Apple ecosystem on macOS. The bridge Blip and Apple Notes are built on.
